title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS)
case: A 45-year-old woman with diabetes wakes 3 times a night with numb thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking her hand. Carpal compression test reproduces symptoms at 15 seconds. Neck exam normal. No wasting. Working diagnosis: mild to moderate CTS. Plan: night splint, tendon and nerve gliding, ergonomic advice, encourage diabetes control through her doctor, reassess at 6 weeks.

differentials.name: C6 or C7 radiculopathy
differentials.key: Neck pain, root pattern, reflex change, no night shaking

differentials.name: Pronator syndrome (median nerve at forearm)
differentials.key: Palm numbness, forearm ache, no night symptoms

differentials.name: Thumb CMC osteoarthritis
differentials.key: Pain at thumb base, grind test positive, no paraesthesia

differentials.name: Peripheral polyneuropathy
differentials.key: Both hands and feet, glove and stocking

qa: Why is the palm usually spared? The palmar cutaneous branch leaves the median nerve before the tunnel.
What finding makes surgery referral urgent? Thenar wasting or constant numbness.
Which conservative treatment has the best support? Night splinting in neutral.
How do you separate CTS from C6 radiculopathy? Neck findings, reflex changes and a root pattern versus night symptoms and wrist provocation.
Why ask about diabetes and thyroid? They increase risk and need medical management.

fields.Therapist: Places both thumbs over the carpal tunnel (just distal to the wrist crease, in the middle)
fields.Action: Apply firm steady pressure for up to 30 seconds
fields.Positive: Tingling or numbness in the median distribution

fields.Position: Sitting; patient presses the backs of the hands together with wrists fully flexed, elbows bent and pointing out
fields.Errors: Allowing the elbows to drop, partial flexion

redFlags.Finding: Sudden severe symptoms after wrist trauma or fracture
Bilateral hand clumsiness with gait change

exercise.Steps: Straight hand, hook fist, full fist, tabletop, straight fist
Wrist and finger extension combined with neck side-flexion toward the arm
Neutral wrist, breaks from forceful gripping, larger tool handles

modalityNotes: Splinting is the best supported conservative treatment. Ultrasound and laser: evidence weak or inconsistent; not routinely recommended. Corticosteroid injection by a doctor may give short- to medium-term relief.
pathway: Track Boston questionnaire, night waking frequency, two-point discrimination, thumb abduction strength. After surgery: early finger movement, scar care, gradual grip loading from about 2 to 4 weeks as advised.
